content: Medical education in the Philippines is primarily provided and developed by accredited and government-recognized medical schools within the country. The Doctor of Medicine (M.D.) degree is a four-year professional program that qualifies graduates to take the licensure examination for medical doctors in the Philippines. Admission to Medical Schools Before applying to medical schools, candidates must first complete a bachelor's degree with credits in specific required subjects. Common pre-medical degrees include biology, psychology, medical technology, pharmacy, nursing, and physical therapy. Additionally, candidates are required to take and pass the National Medical Admissions Test (NMAT), which serves as the national entrance examination for all medical schools in the Philippines. The M.D. program spans four years and focuses on medical theories, practices, technologies, and problem-solving. Completion of this program qualifies graduates to sit for the licensure examination for medical doctors in the Philippines. Regulation of Medical Schools Medical schools in the Philippines are regulated by the Commission on Higher Education (CHED) and accredited by the Association of Philippine Medical Colleges. Notable Medical Schools The top-performing medical schools in the licensure examinations for Filipino doctors include: University of the Philippines College of Medicine Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Maynila, College of Medicine Cebu Institute of Medicine University of Santo Tomas Faculty of Medicine and Surgery Far Eastern University Nicanor Reyes Medical Foundation University of the East Ramon Magsaysay Memorial Medical Center Our Lady of Fatima University Medical Science Foundation De La Salle Health Sciences Campus Licensure Examinations for Physicians The licensure examinations for physicians, also known as the board exams for doctors, are administered by the Board of Medicine, a professional regulatory body under the supervision of the Professional Regulation Commission (PRC) of the Philippines. Advanced Medical Studies After graduating from medical school and passing the licensure examination, Filipino doctors are designated as general medical practitioners. They may pursue further education through graduate programs (e.g., Master of Public Health, Master of Health Services Administration) or specialize in a specific medical field. Graduate medical programs are offered by some medical schools in the Philippines and abroad. These programs typically involve academic lectures, practical exercises, and laboratory work. Requirements may include the presentation and defense of a graduate-level thesis, an independent research project, or supervised professional practice. The duration of these programs ranges from one to five years, depending on the curriculum, institutional demands, and the student's academic load and dedication. Specialization in medicine is overseen by various specialty boards, such as the Philippine Board of Psychiatry, Philippine Board of Pediatrics, Philippine Board of Cardiology, and Philippine Board of Pulmonology, among others. Medical Practice in the Philippines Medical practice in the Philippines is developed, monitored, and regulated by the Philippine Medical Association (PMA), the largest organization of medical doctors in the country. Numerous specialty societies, such as the Philippine College of Family Physicians, Philippine Dermatological Society, Philippine Cancer Society, and Philippine Pediatric Society, also contribute to the regulation and advancement of medical practice. The Department of Health (DOH), a cabinet-level department under the Office of the President of the Philippines, exercises general supervisory powers over medical practitioners and allied health personnel in the country. Notable Filipino Doctors Jose Rizal: The National Hero of the Philippines. Loi Estrada: Former First Lady and Senator of the Philippines. Juan Flavier: Former Health Secretary and Senator of the Philippines. Manuel Dayrit: Former Health Secretary and official of the World Health Organization. Elenita Binay: Former Mayor of Makati City and spouse of former Makati City Mayor Jejomar Binay. Ramon Gustilo: Orthopedic surgeon and co-founder of the Gustilo-Anderson Classification of Open Fractures.
